meta.scope: Japan batch 7 — Social structure and society cluster. Covers the distinctive features of Japan’s super-aged society, long-term care, gender equality, household/poverty/inequality measurement, time-use patterns, and related social statistics. Complements the already-captured demographic (Census, Vital Statistics), employment, immigration, health, education and social-security nodes so that the social dimension of Japan’s uniqueness is adequately represented.
meta.strategy_note: User requested explicit coverage of Japan’s interesting social structure. This batch focuses on high-citation official white papers and fundamental surveys that quantify ageing, care, gender, inequality and daily life. Links tightly to existing Population Census, Vital Statistics, National Health and Nutrition Survey, School Basic Survey, social-security series and foreign-residents nodes.

candidates.title: Annual Report on the Ageing Society / White Paper on the Ageing Society (高齢社会白書)
candidates.description: Statutory annual white paper submitted to the Diet on the state of population ageing, living conditions of older persons, and the implementation of ageing-society measures. Reports the current ageing rate (approximately 29 % of the population aged 65+), future projections, household structure of the elderly, regional differentials, and policy responses including long-term care and employment of older workers.
candidates.notes: Central official narrative and statistical digest of Japan’s super-aged society — the world’s highest ageing rate. Continuously cited in demographic, fiscal, labour and health-policy analysis. Provides the high-level framing that links Population Census / Vital Statistics projections to concrete social and budgetary consequences. Essential node for any graph of Japan’s social structure.

candidates.title: Long-Term Care Insurance (介護保険) statistics and system performance
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW)
candidates.description: Statistics on the Long-Term Care Insurance system introduced in 2000: number of certified persons by care level, service recipients and expenditure by type of service, institutional capacity, workforce, and municipal/prefectural differentials. Includes related series on latter-stage elderly medical care.
candidates.notes: Japan’s distinctive social-insurance response to super-ageing. Benefit costs have more than tripled since introduction and are a major fiscal pressure. Data on certification rates, ‘old-old’ care (老老介護), and service utilisation are heavily cited in ageing-society analysis and in projections of future care workforce needs. Complements the Ageing Society White Paper and the broader social-security series.

candidates.title: White Paper on Gender Equality (男女共同参画白書)
candidates.description: Statutory annual white paper on the status of gender equality and the measures taken to promote a gender-equal society. Covers women’s participation in decision-making, employment and work–life balance, education, health, violence against women, poverty, and regional dimensions. Special features change yearly (e.g., work and health, regional attractiveness, marriage and family).
candidates.notes: Primary official source on gender structure and the persistent gender gap in Japan. Continuously referenced in labour, family, education and political-participation analysis. Provides the policy and statistical frame that links employment surveys, vital statistics (marriage/fertility) and household data to the broader social-structure picture.

candidates.title: Comprehensive Survey of Living Conditions (国民生活基礎調査)
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW)
candidates.description: Large-scale household survey (large-scale every three years, smaller annual) covering household structure, income, savings, health, long-term care, medical expenditure and living conditions. Principal domestic source for relative poverty rates, Gini coefficients (before/after redistribution), elderly single-person households, and ‘old-old’ care arrangements.
candidates.notes: Fundamental social-statistics survey. Supplies the official relative-poverty rate, income-redistribution analysis and detailed household-structure data that underpin discussions of inequality, ageing and social cohesion. Complements the Family Income and Expenditure Survey and National Survey of Family Income and Expenditure already captured in earlier batches.

candidates.title: Survey on Time Use and Leisure Activities (社会生活基本調査)
candidates.description: Quinquennial (and related) survey of how people allocate time across paid work, unpaid work (housework, care), leisure, sleep and other activities, with breakdowns by sex, age, employment status and region. Captures gender division of labour, care burdens and changing lifestyle patterns.
candidates.notes: Key evidence base for the gender division of unpaid work and for discussions of work–life balance, care burdens and changing social norms. Frequently cited alongside the Gender Equality White Paper and employment surveys. Provides behavioural depth that pure labour-force or income statistics cannot.

candidates.title: Survey on the Redistribution of Income / Income redistribution statistics (所得再分配調査)
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW)
candidates.description: Periodic survey and derived statistics that measure income inequality (Gini coefficient) before and after taxes, social-insurance contributions and social-security benefits. Tracks the redistributive effect of Japan’s tax and social-security system across age groups and household types.
candidates.notes: Complements the Comprehensive Survey of Living Conditions. The pre- and post-redistribution Gini series are the standard official measures of how much Japan’s social-security system reduces market-income inequality (especially important given the large elderly population with low market incomes). Directly relevant to fiscal sustainability and social-cohesion analysis.

candidates.title: Basic Act for Gender Equal Society (男女共同参画社会基本法)
candidates.description: Framework law (1999) that establishes the principles and institutional architecture for promoting a gender-equal society and requires the government to submit the annual White Paper on Gender Equality to the Diet.
referenced_by: Every White Paper on Gender Equality
Gender Equality Bureau plans and measures
Diet deliberations and policy evaluations on women’s participation and work–life balance
candidates.notes: Static legal foundation that is recurringly cited as the authority for the annual Gender Equality White Paper and related policy. Parallel to the Statistics Act, Basic Act on Disaster Management and Basic Act on Energy Policy already in the Japan set.

candidates.title: Elderly household structure and living arrangements (from Ageing Society White Paper / Comprehensive Survey of Living Conditions / Census)
candidates.description: Synthesised statistical picture of living arrangements of persons aged 65+: share of single-person elderly households (now over 9 million), elderly-couple-only households, multi-generational households, and the rise of ‘old-old’ care arrangements in which both carer and care recipient are aged 75+. Drawn from the Population Census, Comprehensive Survey of Living Conditions and the Ageing Society White Paper.
candidates.notes: Distinctive structural feature of contemporary Japanese society. The rapid growth of elderly single-person and elderly-couple households, together with old-old care, is repeatedly highlighted in official white papers and is a major driver of long-term-care demand, local-service design and social-isolation policy. Provides the household-level counterpart to the aggregate ageing rate.
